English: Tethered Foal
The humblest beginnings: a few foals roped to posts, watched by young herders. Simple earthworks and makeshift fences mark the start of a horse-breeding tradition.
Open Paddock
A larger, open area surrounded by temporary fencing to allow foals and yearlings to roam. Increased grazing and rudimentary round pens encourage healthy development.
Corral Hut
A central hut stands among sturdy wooden corrals for basic shelter and management. Herding and branding become organized, boosting population growth and manpower.
Breeders Tent
Specialized tents for breeders and senior herdsmen, with fenced-off enclosures for select mares and stallions. Horse health and selective breeding are prioritized.
Grazing Yard
Fenced grazing yards with rotating pastures allow the herd to flourish year-round. Improved fodder storage and water access support greater numbers.
Stallion Pavilion
Grand, timber-framed pavilions house prize stallions and breeding stock. Skilled handlers ensure the finest mounts, and the prestige of the ranch grows.
Mares Room
Sturdy longhouses and warm stables for mares in foal. Skilled midwives and secure birthing pens ensure healthy new generations and a thriving herd.
Stud Hall
A dedicated hall for record-keeping, breeding contracts, and tribute collection. Renowned farriers and veterinarians serve the growing horse population.
Champion Stable
Lavish stables for elite warhorses and racing champions. Trainers from distant lands arrive, and the renown of Magyar horses draws visitors and tribute.
Magyar Grand Ranch
The legendary Grand Ranch: vast stone-walled fields, noble stables, and a great hall. The heart of Magyar horse culture, where the bloodlines of kings are bred and celebrated.
